title: 8-Hour Shift Heap Climb: Retainer Chain vs AbortController Teardown
description: Step through how an un-disconnected MutationObserver and stale closure pin detached DOM subtrees in V8 Old Space until tab OOM.

steps.label: 1. Route Swap Without Observer Teardown (t = 0h 15m)
steps.description: Operator switches between Queue and Telemetry views. Component unmounts, but MutationObserver.disconnect() is never called.
steps.codeHighlight: observer.observe(widgetRoot, { childList: true, subtree: true }); // no cleanup

steps.label: 2. Stale Closure Pins Old State & DOM Refs (t = 2h 00m)
steps.description: The observer callback closes over the mounted component's chartData array and widgetRef, keeping the unmounted React Fiber and its DOM subtree reachable from the browser's C++ observer registry.

steps.label: 3. Major Mark-Sweep Fails to Reclaim (t = 5h 30m)
steps.description: V8 runs full Mark-Compact cycles every 12 seconds. Because the native MutationObserver holds a strong edge to the JS callback, every historical view remains live on the retainer graph.
steps.codeHighlight: // V8 GC trace: 1.4 GB live Old Space, 480 ms stop-the-world pause

steps.label: 4. V8 Heap Limit Reached: Aw, Snap! (t = 7h 45m)
steps.description: Blink tab hits the ~2.4 GB per-renderer V8 heap ceiling. Allocation fails and Chrome terminates the renderer process with RESULT_CODE_HUNG / Out of Memory.
steps.codeHighlight: FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed

steps.label: 5. Fixed Architecture: Unified AbortSignal Lifecycle (t = 8h 00m)
steps.description: A single AbortController in useEffect aborts in-flight telemetry fetches, removes window listeners, and calls observer.disconnect() on signal abort, dropping Old Space back to 128 MB.
